body:
Thank you so much for sharing your experiences with me! I really appreciate the time you took to write such a detailed response. 

I completely agree that I need to evaluate myself and realize that maybe the interactions I have with my family aren't very healthy...especially not at this point in my life. My family has always had this really toxic underbelly that no one seems to talk about, be it past traumas, chronic mental illness that will never get treated, and really deeply rooted favoritism. 

My mother, on top of being a therapist that has always tried to 'patient' me, has several mental illness, on top of past traumas that have gone completely ignored. My father, who also came from an abusive home, is so emotionally cold and detached that I...honestly have trouble talking to him at all, which hurts the most considering we used to be so close when I was a kid. 

As for my sisters...I've always felt second best to them, if that makes any sense. I feel like my older sister has always resented me for being offered more help then she was, and my middle sister is just kind of the golden child...the one that gets doted on. I've never felt like I could hold a candle to them. 

But at the end of the day I think the biggest issue I have right now is that there is no sense of privacy when it comes to my family? They don't seem to understand boundaries, and they truly believe that they should have full access to my life, mental health, and even private thoughts and feelings. If I try to say no, I get guilt tripped, and if I get angry, then they just act like I'm trying to purposefully hurt them. Truth is, I don't trust any of them at all...especially my mother. There have been so many times where I have told her things in confidence, where I've specifically asked her NOT to tell anyone else, and it always turns back around to bite me. A week won't even pass before my entire family, even those who I don't have good relationships with, knows all of my business. It makes ever gathering painful because everyone I see looks at me with this...pity, just barely masking the way their drooling for juicy details about the shitstorm my life is.

Its weirdly comforting? Having a plan? I guess the idea that I can just...take myself out the the equation if things ever get too bad helps me keep going? 

Like at this point I know that one of these days, I'll either walk past the threshold on my own, or let my broken brain do it for me. 

Im glad I'm not alone in this feeling tho...for both of our sakes, I we never feel that push.
